summary: A 1932 Aermotor MC-24 tower with a wooden 14-foot cab on the Fort Apache reservation; the register says it is still active, with no second source found.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-24 tower with a wooden 14-by-14-foot cab and the original ground house

access.note: On the Fort Apache Indian Reservation (tribal land); the register gives no public visiting information.

events.note: Replaced an earlier wooden tower; original ground house remains, per the register

evidence.supports: only Aermotor MC-24 tower on the reservation with a wooden 14x14 cab
evidence.quote: McKay Peak Lookout is the only Aermotor MC-24 tower with wooden 14’ x 14’ cab on the Fort Apache Reservation
It was built in 1932, replacing a wooden tower

evidence.supports: original ground house remains on the site

notes_for_editor: Every history fact rests on one register entry. The 1932 date and wooden cab were not corroborated: a WebSearch found no McKay-specific source, and the MC-24 towers it surfaced nearby were 1933. The 'still active' claim is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land. The register's 'McKay Peak Lookout' title matches the FFLA 'McKay Peak' name; the record's name 'McKay Lookout' is fine. Record coordinates and elevation match the register. Suggest a tribal or BIA records check, or the West Lookouts McKay page if it exists (not cached, not read).
